population.span: We conducted a randomized, double-blind, double-dummy trial comparing two once-daily regimens of edoxaban with warfarin in 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation (median follow-up, 2.8 years).

endpoint.span: The primary efficacy end point was stroke or systemic embolism.

estimate.span: In the intention-to-treat analysis, there was a trend favoring high-dose edoxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio, 0.87; 97.5% CI, 0.73 to 1.04; P=0.08)

ci.span: In the intention-to-treat analysis, there was a trend favoring high-dose edoxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio, 0.87; 97.5% CI, 0.73 to 1.04; P=0.08)

analysis_set.span: In the intention-to-treat analysis, there was a trend favoring high-dose edoxaban versus warfarin

candidate_rejections.why: This served-row provenance describes a derived interval, not a verbatim source result; reject it as the source-bound CI, not the trial or the matching HR.

entry_population_matches_question.why: The registry specifies adults aged at least 21 with documented AF and excludes moderate or severe mitral stenosis and mechanical heart valves; the estimate is explicitly intention-to-treat.
